lesson.title: Der kleine Hund
lesson.subtitle: Anna finds a lost puppy and follows him to the person who misses him

hook.title: Before You Read
hook.content: A small dog is alone in the garden. Anna does not know whose dog he is, so she follows him. Watch the weather at the start and the old man at the end: they tell you what kind of day this is.

footnotes.title: folgen
footnotes.content: folgen = to follow. It takes a dative person: Anna folgt ihm = Anna follows him. You only need to recognise it here.

footnotes.title: Gern geschehen
footnotes.content: Gern geschehen = 'you're welcome' (literally: gladly done). It is the polite answer to danke.

pattern.title: Die Geschichte
pattern.content:
Es ist Samstag. Das Wetter ist schön. Die Sonne scheint, und der Himmel ist blau.

Anna geht in den Garten. Dort sieht sie einen kleinen Hund. Der Hund ist braun und weiß. Er sitzt allein unter einem Baum.

Anna geht langsam zu ihm. „Hallo, kleiner Hund“, sagt sie. Der Hund steht auf und läuft langsam. Anna folgt ihm.

Nach zwei Minuten sehen sie einen alten Mann. Er sitzt auf einer Bank und ist traurig. „Entschuldigung, ist das Ihr Hund?“, fragt Anna. Der Mann lächelt. „Ja! Vielen Dank! Ich habe ihn gesucht.“

Der Hund läuft schnell zu dem Mann. Anna hört, wie der Mann lacht. Sie ist müde, aber sehr froh.

exercises.prompt: Reading check — match each story sentence with its English meaning. Then recall earlier vocabulary in the short phrases:

matching_pairs.english: The dog sits alone under a tree.
matching_pairs.german: Der Hund sitzt allein unter einem Baum.

matching_pairs.english: The old man sits on a bench.
matching_pairs.german: Der alte Mann sitzt auf einer Bank.

matching_pairs.english: Anna is tired but very glad.
matching_pairs.german: Anna ist müde, aber sehr froh.

matching_pairs.english: The baker helps the school pupil

exercises.target_answer: Das Wetter ist schön., Die Sonne scheint., Der Hund sitzt allein unter einem Baum., Anna folgt ihm., Der alte Mann sitzt auf einer Bank., Anna ist müde, aber sehr froh., der Tourist am Flughafen, England ist ein Land, Der Bäcker hilft dem Schüler, der Arbeiter
exercises.meaning: The weather is beautiful.; The sun is shining.; The dog sits alone under a tree.; Anna follows him.; The old man sits on a bench.; Anna is tired but very glad.; the tourist at the airport; England is a country; The baker helps the school pupil; the worker
exercises.explanation: The weather opens the story, the dog moves it, and the old man resolves it. Six beats, one small adventure.

exercises.prompt: Where does Anna find the dog?
exercises.meaning: Anna meets the dog in the garden.
exercises.explanation: The second paragraph begins Anna geht in den Garten. Dort sieht sie einen kleinen Hund.

exercises.prompt: Why is the old man sad?
exercises.meaning: The old man is sad because his dog is missing.
exercises.explanation: The man says Ich habe ihn gesucht — 'I have been looking for him.' His sadness and the dog's return answer the same question.

exercises.prompt: What does Anna hear at the end?
exercises.meaning: Anna hears the old man laugh when the dog returns.
exercises.explanation: The last paragraph says Anna hört, wie der Mann lacht — she hears the man laugh.

exercises.prompt: Which English follows the German words most closely?
exercises.german: Der Hund läuft schnell zu dem Mann.
exercises.natural: The dog runs quickly over to the man.
options: The dog runs fast to the man
The dog runs quickly over to the man
The man runs fast to the dog
The dog slowly leaves the man
exercises.target_answer: The dog runs fast to the man
exercises.meaning: The dog runs fast to the man.
exercises.explanation: zu dem Mann is literally 'to the man' — the dative destination. The natural English 'over to the man' adds a direction word German does not need.

twist.prompt: Without looking back — rebuild: 'The dog sits alone under a tree.'
twist.target_answer: Der Hund sitzt allein unter einem Baum
twist.explanation: unter einem Baum is the dative picture of where the dog sits. The bench (Bank) is a distractor; the story puts the dog under the tree.

summary.outcome: Read a short story about a lost dog and answer where, why, and what-happens questions.

use_example.german: Der Hund sitzt allein unter einem Baum. Anna folgt ihm zu einem alten Mann.
use_example.english: The dog sits alone under a tree. Anna follows him to an old man.

summary.takeaway: Weather and feelings are story clues. A sunny start and a sad old man tell you the problem before the dialogue names it.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Next branch: a train, rain, and a wrong bus in Paris.

sonne.etymology_derivation: Old High German sunna — shares Proto-Germanic *sun(n)uz with English sun. [wiktionary]

bank.context_translation: I am going to the bank.
bank.etymology_derivation: The money-changers bench: Bank is the Germanic twin of English bench (Proto-Germanic *bankiz), and the financial sense came through Italian banca. [wiktionary]

entschuldigung.context_translation: Excuse me, where is the station?
entschuldigung.etymology_derivation: entschuldigen + -ung — the 'un-guilting' noun; the page names no English cognates. [wiktionary]

laufen.context_phrase: Ich laufe jeden Morgen im Park.
laufen.context_translation: I run every morning in the park.
laufen.etymology_derivation: Class 7 strong verb from Proto-West Germanic *hlaupan - the exact relative of English leap and lope; läuft-lief-gelaufen preserves the old ablaut. [wiktionary]

froh.context_phrase: Ich bin froh, dass du kommst.
froh.context_translation: I am glad that you are coming.
froh.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *frawaz 'quick, glad' — English frolic (via Dutch) is the named cognate. [wiktionary]

hören.etymology_derivation: From Middle High German hœren, from Old High German hōren. English hear is a listed cognate. [wiktionary]

himmel.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *himil — the same Germanic line as English heaven's root family. [wiktionary]

minute.etymology_derivation: Medieval Latin minūta — the same Latin loan as English minute. [wiktionary]

scheinen.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *skīnan — class 1 strong verb (schien, geschienen), ablaut-matching shine/shone. [wiktionary]

hund.context_phrase: Der Hund schläft auf dem Sofa.
hund.context_translation: The dog sleeps on the sofa.
hund.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *hundaz — cognate with English hound, the same ancient dog-word. [wiktionary]

garten.context_translation: The children play in the garden.

baum.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *baumaz — English beam is the cognate; a beam was originally a tree. [wiktionary]

alt.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *aldaz — the twin of old; the l stayed, the vowel and final d/t report the shift. [wiktionary]

mann.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *mann- — the identical twin of man; German keeps the short a English lengthened. [wiktionary]

frau.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *frawjǭ 'lady, mistress' — kin to archaic English frow 'lady'; Fräulein andMs.-style Frauennamen carry the same root. [wiktionary]

süß.context_phrase: Der Kuchen ist zu süß für mich.
süß.context_translation: The cake is too sweet for me.
süß.etymology_derivation: süß — from Proto-Germanic *swōtuz, PIE *swéh₂dus, exactly cognate with English sweet; the final t shifted to ß and the old w was lost before the rounded vowel. [wiktionary]

müde.context_phrase: Ich bin müde und gehe ins Bett.
müde.context_translation: I am tired and go to bed.
müde.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *mōþī; only Dutch moe named — no English cognate, memorize this one. [wiktionary]

glücklich.etymology_derivation: Glück (luck) + -lich; Wiktionary: 'Compare English luck' — a relative via Dutch. [wiktionary]

allein.etymology_derivation: Middle High German al-ein, literally all one — the identical compound that formed English alone (Middle English al-one). [wiktionary]

sitzen.shift_rule: T → S / SS / Z + Ablaut Vowels
sitzen.context_translation: We are sitting in the café.

stehen.context_phrase: Ich stehe am Fenster und sehe hinaus.
stehen.context_translation: I stand at the window and look out.
stehen.etymology_derivation: From Proto-Germanic *stāną; the page documents cognate English stand, the same stand-verb family (English stood, German stand). [wiktionary]

danke.etymology_derivation: Ellipsis of ich danke dir — the same danken already known (the think/thank family, th→d). [wiktionary]

helfen.etymology_derivation: p → f. Governs the dative case (mir).

finden.context_translation: I cannot find it / I find it not.
finden.etymology_derivation: Stem find + infinitive -en (German keeps pure short [ɪ] vowel).

suchen.context_translation: I am looking for my glasses.
suchen.etymology_derivation: k → ch. Direct transitive object without prepositions.
